sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the test tools, the chase win model types, and all the calibration functions the tests use.
sections.why: Gives the tests every function they call.

sections.name: calibratedMatches
sections.title: Synthetic match sample builder
sections.what: Builds a list of predictions for a set of matches. Each match contributes three predictions that share one outcome, with an optional shift that mimics bad calibration.
sections.why: Likely reason: a match is the unit that counts in these tests, so each match should be counted once.
sections.watch_out: The shift parameter simulates a biased model. Keep it at zero for tests that expect a calibrated result.

sections.name: match-level calibration (calibration) (part 1)
sections.title: Buckets, pass and counting checks
sections.what: Checks the random source, merging of buckets until each has enough matches, that a calibrated model passes and a shifted one fails, that each match counts once, and that Brier arithmetic is correct.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single long match should not dominate the result.
sections.watch_out: The minimum match count per bucket controls how easily a model passes.

sections.name: match-level calibration (calibration) (part 2)
sections.title: Logistic fit, simulated chase and walk-forward
sections.what: Checks that the logistic fit recovers the known slope and intercept, that a simulated chase wins at the rate the model predicts, that ties are settled by a coin, and that the walk-forward intercept uses earlier dates only.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms that each day is scored only with information from before it.
sections.watch_out: The walk-forward test expects exact rounding. Changing the learning rate or the rounding will fail it.

sections.name: match-level calibration (calibration) (part 3)
sections.title: Calibration line and slope test
sections.what: Checks that a calibrated sample has an intercept near zero and a slope near one. Checks that the joint test rejects a shifted sample and refuses to pass a sample with only one match.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single match cannot show calibration, so the test should fail rather than pass by default.
sections.watch_out: Degenerate samples are rejected on purpose. Relaxing that rule would let a bad model pass.

summary: Checks the match-level calibration statistics: buckets, Brier scores, logistic fits, a simulated chase, the walk-forward adjustment, and the calibration line and slope test.
purpose: Verifies the statistical engine behind the calibration gates, so the saved results can be trusted.
why: Likely reason: the gates decide whether a model is trusted, so their maths must be proven on known cases first.
how: Creates synthetic match samples with seeded randomness. Tests bucket merging, pass and fail for calibrated and shifted samples, match counting, logistic fitting, the simulated chase, the walk-forward date rules, and the calibration line and slope test.
inputs: Synthetic samples and an outcome distribution from the chaseWp module.
risks: Several tests run bootstrap resamples, which are slow and depend on seeds. Numeric tolerances may need updating if the algorithm changes.
debug: Start with the first failing test name. Check whether the match count and the ball count are being mixed up, and check the seed value used.
